  Algorithmic Graph Theory [MAT_4341]  
  Marks: 50                                                                               Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  $$1)           The transpose of a directed graph G= (V, E) is the graph GT = (V, ET) where ET = {(v,$$  
  u): (u, v) is in E}. Describe an efficient algorithm for computing GT from G when the      (3)  
  adjacency matrix representation of G is given.  
  A)  
  B)      Design an algorithm to find diameter of a tree T. Analyse the running time of your  
  algorithm.                                                                                 (3)  
  
  C)      Write an algorithm to check if a given graph is bipartite. Analyse the time complexity of  
  your algorithm.                                                                           (4)  
  
  2)           Suppose we define a different kind of graph G = (V, E) where we have positive weights  
  on the vertices and not on the edges. Given a starting vertex v find the lowest-cost path  
  from v to every other vertex. The cost of a path is the sum of the weights of the vertices (3)  
  A)      on the path.  
  Modify Dijkstra's algorithm to find shortest path from v to every other vertex.  
  
  B)      Write the steps of Bellman-Ford algorithm and analyse its time complexity.                 (3)  
  C)      Write down the steps of Kruskal's algorithm to find minimum spanning tree in a  
  weighted undirected graph. Analyse its time complexity.                                    (4)  
  
  3)           (I) Prove that a directed graph is acyclic if and only if a depth search of G yields no back  
  edge.  
  (II) Let T be a tree with maximum degree k. Prove that T has at least k vertices of degree (4)  
  A)      1.  
  
  B)      Prove that Hamiltonian Cycle problem in a graph is NP-Complete.                            (3)  
  C)      Write an algorithm to check whether a given graph is Eulerian. Analyse its time  
  complexity.                                                                                (3)
